text:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: 5xx spike detected for /v1/generate in eu-west-1, error-rate 12% over 5m. Smart-router started fallbacks to model:rw-small-quant.

amanda: @here paging SRE, I see error surge and a bunch of requests routed to rw-small-quant. Can someone confirm if the fallback policy is misconfiged?

raj: on it. looking at routing logs now. quick question — are these customer-facing errors or internal transform failures?

sophia: Support queue reporting multiple customer complaints about garbled outputs and timeouts. Customer impact: several PLG customers report 20-30% request failures.

jules: I can take oncall handoff if needed. amanda, do you want me to try a targeted rollback of the fallback policy? last rollout was 01:12 UTC.

amanda: yes, please. But do NOT force a region-wide pin yet. There was an earlier incident where force-region caused a routing loop. Try a policy tweak first.

raj: policy dump attached:
```
smart-routing: {
  prefer_latency: true,
  fallbacks: [rw-long-quant, rw-small-quant],
  override_rules: [{when: "capacity_shortage", action: "fallback"}]
}
```
Looks normal. However the router is marking rw-small-quant as compatible for a broader set of requests — causing high fanout.

sophia: Support: customers A and D are impacted; ticket IDs #4579 #4581. High severity.

jules: I'm going to temporarily reduce fallback weight to rw-small-quant to 10% and increase rw-long-quant to 90% via hotpatch. If that doesn't help we'll roll back the new fallback order.

amanda: make the change and post the exact command. keep me in the loop.

jules: running:
```
curator-cli modify-fallback --env=prod --region=eu-west-1 --model-weight rw-small-quant=10 --model-weight rw-long-quant=90 --note="hotpatch reduce small-quant fanout"
```

infra-bot: Command queued: curator-cli (id: c1234). Applying changes in 20s.

pagerduty-bot: @amanda @jules acknowledged incident P-3129. Escalation to L2 if not mitigated in 10m.

jules: changes applied. Observability: error-rate dropped to 6% but latency spiked for some customers.

raj: getting mixed signals. Some routes are still pinned to rw-small-quant because of a manual override present from earlier today:
```
route-status --region eu-west-1 --route /v1/generate
> route: /v1/generate
  pinned_variant: rw-small-quant (manual-pin by amanda @ 2034565000)
```

amanda: oh — that's my manual pin from earlier debugging. I forgot I left it. My bad. That pin would override the hotpatch weights and explain the residual failures.

sophia: That pin is affecting high-traffic customers. Can we unpin just that route?

jules: I can remove the pin, but note: removing pin will trigger immediate traffic rebalancing. Do we want a controlled drain?

raj: Controlled drain please. Do `drain-window=60s` and monitor.

jules: running unpin with drain:
```
curator-cli unpin-route --route=/v1/generate --region=eu-west-1 --drain=60
```

infra-bot: Unpin job started (job id u-987). Drain in progress.

sophia: Support: notifying affected customers that we're mitigating and expect improved behavior within 5 minutes. "We're investigating routing issues; temporary service disruption possible." Sent messages to Customer A & D.

jules: drain completed. Observability shows fallback distribution now respecting weights. 5xx down to 1.2% and latency returning to baseline.

amanda: thanks. Really sorry for leaving that manual-pin active — I should have documented it in the incident channel before stepping away.

raj: action item: we should block manual pins from bypassing hotpatches or at least flag them in the console. This is a recurring footgun.

sophia: Support will follow up with customers with post-incident notes and timeline.

jules: I'll open a postmortem draft and include timeline, commands, and recommended change: "disallow manual pins without TTL or add explicit UI warning." Assigning to infra team.

amanda: assign me as author for the postmortem. Also I'll create a short runbook section on pin hygiene.

pagerduty-bot: Incident P-3129 auto-resolved by user actions. Closing alert in 2m unless reopened.

support-bot: Tickets #4579 #4581 updated with mitigation and ETA for RCA.

amanda: summary: cause = leftover manual-pin to rw-small-quant that overrode fallback-hotpatch; mitigation = reduced fallback weight + unpin with drain; impact = several PLG customers saw degraded outputs ~30m; follow-ups = postmortem, pin TTL/restrictions, UI warning. Great teamwork, thanks everyone :clap:

raj: filing RFC for safer override semantics. +1 on TTLs and permissions.

jules: will add the exact commands and timings to the postmortem. Closing thread after docs posted.

infra-bot: Reaction summary: :thumbsup: amanda, :eyes: raj, :white_check_mark: jules, :warning: support-bot.
